stories.title: Chinese open‑weight AI models show fingerprints of U.S. export‑banned Nvidia Blackwell GPUs
stories.summary: A research analysis by Will DePue of Unemployment Labs found that open‑weight large language models released by Chinese firms—including DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax, and Ant Group—contain weight patterns that match training on Nvidia’s Blackwell GPUs, which are prohibited from export to China. The study cites fingerprint evidence in Moonshot’s Kimi K3 and DeepSeek’s V4 models, indicating the chips were used despite U.S. export controls.

stories.previousTitle: Chinese open‑weight AI models show evidence of training on U.S.-banned Nvidia Blackwell GPUs
stories.previousSummary: A study by Will DePue of the nonprofit Unemployment Labs examined the weight matrices of open‑weight large language models released by DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax and Ant Group. The analysis identified patterns that match the configurations of Nvidia’s Blackwell GPUs, which are prohibited from export to China. The article also notes that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang left the company after an affair was disclosed, and that Nvidia may still ship its less powerful H200 chip to China via a circuitous route permitted under existing export rules.

stories.title: Nvidia posts worst weekly decline since 2018 Trump tariff sell‑off as CEO Jensen Huang exits
stories.summary: Nvidia’s shares recorded their steepest weekly loss since the 2018 market sell‑off triggered by Trump‑era tariffs. The decline occurred in the same week that the company announced the departure of its chief executive Jensen Huang. The stock’s performance marked a notable reversal after a period of strong gains.

stories.title: FICCI urges India‑Africa comprehensive trade framework
stories.summary: FICCI urged India and African nations to negotiate a comprehensive, predictable trade framework aimed at lowering barriers and encouraging investment. Secretary General Anant Swarup said the two regions should explore a broader arrangement, and the call comes as Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal prepares to visit Egypt, a strategic hub for Indian companies.
stories.why: A formal framework could expand bilateral commerce and investment, supporting economic growth in both regions.
stories.previousTitle: FICCI calls for comprehensive India‑Africa trade framework ahead of minister’s Egypt visit
stories.previousSummary: The Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) urged India and African nations to develop a comprehensive trade arrangement that would provide a predictable framework, reduce barriers and attract investment. FICCI Secretary General Anant Swarup highlighted the need for broader cooperation. The call was made as Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal prepares for a visit to Egypt, which FICCI sees as an opportunity to strengthen ties.

stories.title: India and US resolve most trade deal issues, pact could be sealed soon, says Jaishankar
stories.summary: Indian Foreign Minister S. Jaishankar said that India and the United States have resolved the bulk of outstanding issues in their proposed trade agreement and that the pact could be sealed in the near future. His comment indicates that negotiations have moved past major sticking points.
